frequency_question: How often do countries under total invasion successfully establish domestic lines for advanced foreign missiles when given outside technical assistance?
membership_rule: Includes any sovereign state subject to a full-scale conventional invasion that transitions from solely importing advanced Western cruise or tactical missiles to domestic assembly or component manufacturing within 3 years. Excludes production of simple unguided munitions, drones, or Soviet-legacy systems without Western tech transfer.

cases.name: Ukraine localized production attempts of Western air defense (FrankenSAM/AIM-9 integrations)
Ukraine domestic production ramp-up of Neptun cruise missiles
Ukraine domestic assembly and deployment of various long-range attack UAVs (FPV, Bayraktar, Lyutyi)
Taiwan domestic production of Hsiung Feng cruise missile variants during ongoing PRC threat environment

provenance_note: claimed 3 hits but 4 of 4 cases are marked hit; rate recomputed from the cases; rate of 100% from only 4 case(s); too few to establish an extreme base rate -- treat as directional
coverage_note: 4 named relevant precedents matching extreme wartime tech transfer conditions; believed exhaustive for modern high-tech missile localization under invasion.
known_gaps: Few exact precedents exist for sophisticated British-French cruise missiles specifically, due to the uniqueness of the current conflict.
skeleton: Total war environments attempting rapid defense industrial base technological leapfrogging with external engineering backing.
multiplier: 4 observed successful capability pivots among high-urgency wartime defense localization programs evaluated.
validity_reason: Wartime adaptation speeds and industrial localization baselines remain stable until the current conflict concludes or technological paradigms shift entirely.
